title: U.S. Geological Survey global seabed mineral resources
citation: U.S. Geological Survey, 2025, U.S. Geological Survey global seabed mineral resources: U.S. Geological Survey Fact Sheet FS-2025-3017, map scale 1:103,450,000.
notes: Four-page global fact sheet on seabed mineral resources (all pages have pdf_text; no OCR needed). It describes no named stratigraphic units, borings, wells, structures or aquifers in South Carolina; its only South Carolina content is a mention of ecosystem work on the Blake Plateau off South Carolina (page 1). Seabed mineral types in table 1 (polymetallic nodules, sulfides, crusts, phosphorite, heavy mineral sands) are commodity classes, not map units, and were not recorded as units. Only references relevant to South Carolina offshore or the map's prospective regions were recorded; general references (Burton 2022; Gartman and others 2022 on Alaska; Hein and others 2005 on the Pacific; Pearsall 2022 on Escanaba Trough; U.S. Department of State 2023; USGS 2022a critical minerals list; USGS 2025 extended continental shelf) were skipped. Reference entries are two-column on page 4; citations were read across the interleaved lines.
